events: net.neoforged.neoforge.network.event.RegisterPayloadHandlersEvent (mod bus, added via getModEventBus().addListener inside onInitialize)
keybinds: key.vanillaplusadditions.item_vault_viewer.open_modifier — default Left Ctrl (GLFW_KEY_LEFT_CONTROL, InputConstants.Type.KEYSYM), category key.categories.vanillaplusadditions; en_us: "Open Item Vault Viewer (hold + right-click vault)", de_de: "Item-Vault-Viewer öffnen (halten + Rechtsklick auf Vault)". It is a hold-modifier, not a press action — read via raw GLFW window state (InputConstants.isKeyDown / glfwGetMouseButton), not KeyMapping.isDown(); rebindable to a mouse button too.
oneLiner: Hold Ctrl and right-click a Create Item Vault while wearing Engineering Goggles to see everything stored inside it in a searchable, sortable read-only grid — including vaults mounted on moving contraptions, where Create itself opens nothing.

requiredMods.evidence: src/main/java/net/geraldhofbauer/vanillaplusadditions/modules/item_vault_viewer/ItemVaultViewerModule.java:53-56 — `protected boolean shouldInitialize() { return isCreateLoaded(); }`, with `isCreateLoaded()` = `ModList.get().isLoaded("create")` at :49-51. Every packet handler re-checks it (:68, :109) and every client handler checks it first (ItemVaultViewerClientEvents.java:46, :92; ItemVaultViewerClientSetup.java:16). Note the bundle's neoforge.mods.toml declares create as type="optional" (lines 80-87) — the module simply no-ops without it.

shortDescription: Lets players view Create Item Vault contents with Engineering Goggles.
notes:
REGISTERED CONTENT (no items/blocks/entities): the module registers exactly one MenuType, `vanillaplusadditions:item_vault_viewer` (ItemVaultViewerModule.java:34-38), plus two C2S payloads on registrar "1": `vanillaplusadditions:open_item_vault_viewer` (placed vault) and `vanillaplusadditions:open_contraption_vault_viewer` (contraption vault). The DeferredRegister is only bound to the mod bus inside `onInitialize()` (module:60), so without Create the MenuType is never registered at all - and `ItemVaultViewerClientSetup` guards its `.get()` with `isCreateLoaded()` (line 16) so nothing NPEs.

NO MODULE CONFIG AT ALL. `ItemVaultViewerConfig` is a 10-line class that only calls `super(module)` and does not override `buildModuleSpecificConfig`. Only the universal `enabled` / `debug_logging` keys from `AbstractModuleConfig` (:58-66) exist. `enabledByDefault` = true comes from the interface default `Module.isEnabledByDefault()` (core/Module.java:73-75); neither the module nor its config overrides it.

READ-ONLY IN THE STRICTEST SENSE: `ItemVaultViewerMenu` adds **zero** Slots (not even the player inventory) and `quickMoveStack` returns `ItemStack.EMPTY` (menu:155-157). Nothing can be taken out, shift-clicked or moved. The `playerInventory` constructor parameter is therefore unused - intentional, but it looks odd to a reader.

SNAPSHOT, NOT LIVE: the whole content list, `totalSlots`, `occupiedSlots` and `fillFraction` are computed server-side once in `readContents()` (module:194-216) and written into the open-menu payload (module:165-174). There is no tick handler and no refresh path anywhere in the module, so the GUI shows a frozen snapshot from the moment of opening - a vault being filled by a machine while the GUI is open will look unchanged. Doc writers should not promise "live view".

MERGED STACKS CAN EXCEED MAX STACK SIZE: `collectStacks` (module:218-238) merges by `ItemStack.isSameItemSameComponents` and calls `existing.grow(...)` without clamping, so one displayed stack represents the whole vault total (e.g. 3200 cobblestone in one cell). The GUI shrinks the count font at >=100 (0.85x) and >=1000 (0.72x) to keep it readable (screen:335).

FILL BAR MATHS (module:194-216): fill is counted in *stack units* - per slot `count / max(1, min(slotLimit, maxStackSize))`, each slot clamped to 1.0 - not in slots. A slot with 32 cobblestone counts as half full, a slot with one shulker box as completely full. Slot counts are reported separately and only shown in the bar's hover tooltip (screen:200-220). `formatPercent` (screen:273-283) deliberately never prints 0% or 100% unless the vault is truly empty/full (rounds to 1% / 99% instead). Bar colour: green, yellow from 70%, red from 90% (screen:248-256). Added in v1.0.0-beta.69 (CHANGELOG:428-448); that release also changed the menu wire format (anchor -> fill numbers -> stacks) and the CHANGELOG explicitly warns that client and server must run the same version.

ALL GUI TEXT IS HARDCODED ENGLISH. The only lang key this module owns is the keybind (en_us.json:144 / de_de.json:144 - a repo-wide grep for `item_vault_viewer` in resources finds nothing else). The window title is `Component.literal("Item Vault Viewer")` (module:163) and the screen hardcodes "Search", "Desc"/"Asc", "No matches", "Empty", "Vault N% full", "N / M slots used", "N items". None of that is translatable.

KEYBIND IS REGISTERED UNCONDITIONALLY: `ItemVaultViewerKeybinds.onRegisterKeyMappings` (keybinds:31-34) has no `isCreateLoaded()` and no module-enabled check, so the mapping appears in the Controls screen even without Create installed or with the module disabled. Every *use* of it is gated, so it is harmless but visible.

DEBUG LOGGING: the module's `debug_logging` config key controls NOTHING here - on either side. `ItemVaultViewerModule` never calls `getConfig().shouldDebugLog()` (other modules such as death_coordinates and hostile_zombified_piglins do), and `AbstractModule.getLogger()` is a plain `LoggerFactory.getLogger(this.getClass())` (AbstractModule.java:38). The server-side `getLogger().debug(...)` calls (module:114-152) and the client-side `[IVV/contraption]` diagnostics from `ItemVaultViewerClientEvents`' own logger (clientEvents:39, 183-185) are therefore equivalent: both appear only if the log4j DEBUG level is enabled for those logger names. (An earlier draft of this sheet claimed the server-side calls honour `debug_logging` - they do not.)

HEAVY REFLECTION, SILENT ON FAILURE (placed vaults): `getController()` reflects `getControllerBE()`, `getInventory()` reflects the **protected** field `itemCapability` and falls back to the method `getInventoryOfBlock()` (module:240-269). Verified against the vendored jar: `javap -p libs/create-1.21.1-6.0.9.jar` shows `protected ICapabilityProvider<IItemHandler> itemCapability`, `public ItemVaultBlockEntity getControllerBE()` and `public ItemStackHandler getInventoryOfBlock()` on `ItemVaultBlockEntity` - so all three targets exist in the shipped Create version. All three swallow `ReflectiveOperationException` and return null, which the handler treats as "just don't open". A Create rename will make the viewer silently stop working on placed vaults with no log line at all.

CONTRAPTION PATH IS THE FRAGILE ONE: `ContraptionVaultAccess` first reads the `Controller` stamp from the captured block-entity NBT (:149-155); if absent it reflects the **protected** field `Contraption.capturedMultiblocks` (:161-182; javap confirms `protected Multimap<BlockPos, StructureBlockInfo> capturedMultiblocks`); if that fails too it warns ONCE (`warnedReflection` latch) and falls back to "nearest mounted storage within Chebyshev radius 3" (:76-88) - which can show a neighbouring vault's contents rather than the clicked one. Members are sorted to mirror Create's own member order (`ItemVaultBlockEntity.initCapability`, which javap confirms is private in Create), i.e. a behavioural coupling to Create internals, not an API.

WHY MULTIBLOCK CONTRAPTION VAULTS NEEDED SPECIAL CODE: a multiblock vault has no shared inventory; each block keeps its own 20 slots and Create's assembly mounts each block as its own storage. Reading a single storage showed at most 1/20 of the vault (the beta.59 bug, CHANGELOG:698-710). Documented at length in `ContraptionVaultAccess`'s class javadoc.

CONTRAPTION CLICKS DO NOT FIRE RightClickBlock - Create routes them through `InputEvent.InteractionKeyMappingTriggered`. The module hooks that at `EventPriority.HIGH` (before Create's handler) and mirrors Create's own lookup exactly (`ContraptionHandlerClient.getRayInputs`, `ContraptionHandler.loadedContraptions`, `ContraptionHandlerClient.rayTraceContraption`). It only cancels when the hit block really is a vault; anything else falls through to Create untouched.

GATES, AND WHICH SIDE ENFORCES WHAT: client-only (the server cannot see them) are the held modifier key, main-hand-only and - in the contraption path - `player.isSpectator()`; the placed-block client handler has no spectator check. Server-side both packet handlers re-check module-enabled, `isCreateLoaded()`, goggles worn (`GogglesItem.isWearingGoggles`), not sneaking, that the target really is a vault, and a 64-block range (`distanceToSqr > 64.0*64.0`). The same 64-block range plus the vault check is re-tested every tick in `Anchor.stillValid()` (menu:32-67), so the GUI closes on walking away or on disassembly of the contraption.

POSSIBLE CONFLICT WITH THE PROJECT'S OWN OPTIONAL-MOD-GATE RULE: the gate method `isCreateLoaded()` lives in `ItemVaultViewerModule` itself, a class whose imports and method bodies reference Create types (`ItemVaultBlock`, `GogglesItem`, `AbstractContraptionEntity`), and the module is constructed unconditionally in `VanillaPlusAdditions.java:169`. The project memory note "Optional-Mod-Gates & Linking" says a gate must sit in a class free of optional-mod types. CHANGELOG line 974 (beta.25/beta.30 work) explicitly claims "`item_vault_viewer` war bereits sauber isoliert" and reports a verified boot on a bare NeoForge server, so it has evidently been tested - but the arrangement contradicts the written rule and is worth flagging before anyone refactors it.

STANDALONE JAR DECLARES NO CREATE DEPENDENCY: the standalone entrypoint is `standalone/item_vault_viewer/ItemVaultViewerStandalone.java` (`@Mod("vpa_item_vault_viewer")`, delegating to `StandaloneModuleBootstrap.boot(new ItemVaultViewerModule(), ...)`), and the jar is declared in build.gradle:443 with no mixins, no dataGlobs and no moduleDeps. `renderModuleToml` (build.gradle:507-528) emits only `vpa_core`, `neoforge`, `minecraft`, any `moduleDeps` and an `incompatible` entry against the bundle - so `vpa_item_vault_viewer` does not mention Create at all, not even as optional, and simply no-ops when Create is absent. The bundle's own `META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml` does declare `create` as `optional`, versionRange `[6.0,)`, ordering AFTER, side BOTH (lines 80-87).

BUILD: Create is wired as `implementation files("libs/create-1.21.1-6.0.9.jar")` (build.gradle:127) - that jar is NOT gitignored (`git check-ignore` reports nothing; .gitignore:72-75 lists only sable/ToughAsNails/Quark/Zeta) but is also not committed, so it has to be present locally to compile this module.

FEATURE TIMELINE (git tags are authoritative here, the CHANGELOG headings are one release off in two places): the module was added in commit a826414 (2026-06-17), and tag **v1.0.0-beta.13 points exactly at that commit** - although the CHANGELOG lists "Item Vault Viewer Modul" under `[1.0.0-beta.14]` (CHANGELOG:1029). The hold-to-peek Ctrl modifier came with commit ec47f31 (2026-07-05), filed under `[1.0.0-beta.30]` in the CHANGELOG (:954) - but **there is no v1.0.0-beta.30 tag**; the earliest tag containing that commit is v1.0.0-beta.31. Before it, the viewer hijacked every right-click. Contraption support shipped in commit e0eb358 / v1.0.0-beta.58 but was non-functional until the two fixes in v1.0.0-beta.59 (client ray trace + server multi-storage read). The fill-level bar and its tooltip landed in the v1.0.0-beta.69 release commit 5f5fd49, replacing the old `1-6 / 12` pagination readout in the header.

NO DOCS PAGE EXISTS YET: `grep -rl item_vault_viewer docs/` returns nothing and there is no `docs/modules/item_vault_viewer.md`. The only prose is the README paragraph (README.md:172-173) and the optional-mod table row (README.md:224). The README row wording "Module skips initialization entirely" is accurate.

NO TODO/FIXME comments and no dead code found in the module directory (10 files).
